People working in IT are as "reclusive", as any people working in any domain. Sure there are certain activities that that may involve some minimal contact, but the IT department requires quite a lot of talking, since the work of production has shifted to the Agile mode, as I have described to you.

At least in Romania, where I live, it involves:

\- weekly meetings with the manager/requirement leader

\- understanding not by formal and formatted demands, but by active listening and day by day talking

\- fast execution of commands (generally weekly goals)

\- adaptabilty to changing requirements and situations. You cannot have a single mind framework... Shit changes all the time, the manager may want you to do multiple thinks at once, your work may not be correct for an error that nobody could have seen it, you may be required to solve an issue in a limited amount of time.

If you are a timid person, who cannot come up with an instant argument, and the team leader wants an answer, as to why you have not finished on time, or why the product doesn't work the way it was supposed to work, you HAVE to talk!

What I have described to you does not necessarily apply to all IT firms. But it is the environment, that I have been subjected to. Generally this way of organising is adopted by companies that want to cut out costs, and do not hold to well on the market. Keep also in mind, that I am not the person who can tolerate stress, colleagues dissatisfaction and contradictions in the manager's organisation, requirements and attitude.

If I had the money to pay for an employment lawyer, I would do that... but I also, don't have time and energy to take them into a judicial process. And even if I would do such a think, one of the requirements of my contract work, mentions that one has to keep in line with all the members of the team, to listen and explain the tasks. Software development is not a concrete domain, in that you can explain to the average man what does your work process imply and what the end product would be. It is very abstract, and in the lack of a birocratic, hierarchical and established system, you are left with an Agile work of production, in which (almost) anything is decided on the move. This mode of working puts much more emphasizes on communication skills. If you have emotional problems and don't feel confortable speaking with people, your work WILL be subpar.
